description.narrative: The development objective of Social Assistance Project for Lesotho is to support the Government of Lesotho in improving the efficiency and equity of selected social assistance programs. This project has two components. 1) The first component, Strengthening administrative efficiency and equity of social assistance programs, aims to support the results in efficiency and equity of selected social assistance programs, in line with the National Social Protection Strategy (NSPS) and its implementation framework. 2) The second component, Implementation Support, aims to support the investment necessary to overcome the main constraints in term of capacity, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of results supported by first component and to support the design and implementation of a pilot of livelihood enhancement activities among beneficiaries of social assistance programs to support further household's income generating capacity in the medium and long term. It has three subcomponents as follows: (i) Supporting the achievement of results in selected social assistance programs; (b) Supporting the design and implementation of a pilot of livelihoods enhancement activities; and (iii) Supporting the project management.

The objective of the Project is to support the GoL in improving the efficiency, equity and shock responsive function of selected Social Assistance programs and, in the event of an Eligible Crisis or Emergency, to provide immediate and effective response to said Eligible Crisis or Emergency.

title.narrative: PDI 1: Number of non-eligible beneficiaries eliminated from the OAP roster.

comment.narrative:
<p>Efficiency indicator, surpassed. Confirmed by Gov. Final Report. Includes monthly rolling deletions 2018/19, deletions as a result of the PoL 2019/20, but not yet including deletions from when GOLSABS was launched in May 2021 and fully used for payment in June2021. Number may be even higher and can be updated. Each OAP beneficiary has a unique identifier, and is a legal requirement. UsingID card as unique identifier will help further optimize the list and remove duplications.</p>
<p>The indicator is a net indicator of the number of beneficiaries taken off the program. Program shrunk from about 85,000 to approx. 79,000.</p>

title.narrative: Number of annual meetings of the Social Protection Policy Committee
Percentage of OAP beneficiaries with a yearly proof of life verification

actual.value: All accounts in the OAP has had a PoL in Nov 2019-January 2020. 100% of OAP pensioners on the June 2021 paylist were seen in personand the new MIS GOLSABS system has been upgraded to require pensioners to be seen once per year from now on. It was launched and used for the payroll in June 2021.

title.narrative: Percentage of new beneficiaries of PA and OVC entered in the calendar year selected using the harmonized targeting procedures adopted in Year 1

actual.value: OVC: 100% (2047 new beneficiaries selected using NISSA) PA: 0% (no new beneficiaries)

title.narrative: A new more secure payment system is developed, including different modalities, and a pilot is implemented

comment.narrative:
<p>This RI was revised from <strong>"Percentage of OAP beneficiaries paid through an electronic payment system"</strong> to <strong>"A new more secure payment system is developed, including different modalities, and a pilot is implemented"</strong> in the restructuring of November 2019.</p>
<p>Revised indicator target partially achieved.</p>

actual.value: Second phase of enhanced cash pilot was implemented in Mohale's Hoek 9-13 November 2020. In Qacha's Nek, 25-31 October 2020 there was continuation of data cleaning.

title.narrative: Percentage of community councils in the country covered by NISSA-CBT registry

comment.narrative: <p>Indicator covers only rural community councils. 100% achieved and in addition, NISSA was rolled out also to all urban districts.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of payments to CGPand PA paid through the unified payment system

comment.narrative:
<p>Reported at 100% achieved, but with caveat.</p>

<p>100% paid through same agents and same pay points, PA payment module exists in the system (not yet used as people enrolled but not yet received funding)All CGP payments (over 50,000 in December) and all PA uses the same payment agent (G4S or mobile) and all pay points are the same. PA module is there in the MIS; PA should only be forpoor and ultra-poor households without children. Around 12,000 PA beneficiaries still paid manually because of targeting differences with CGP beneficiaries.
 </p>

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator was revised from "Percentage of beneficiaries..." to "Percentage of OVC and CGP beneficiary children who hold the unique ID number provided by Home Affairs (percentage)" in the November 2019 restructuring.</p>

title.narrative: Number of meetings of the Social Protection Technical Committees for Childhood and Old Age
Number of meetings of the Social Protection Technical Committees for Childhood and Old Age

comment.narrative: <p>This is a general indicator, pertaining to both  Equity and Efficiency. Surpassed, Confirmed by Gov. Final Report, and includes only the CGP program. Revised target at the time of the AF.</p>

<p>General indicator (Equity/Efficiency), Confirmed, Surpassed. This covers the CGP and OAP programs (PA, OVC…). Should be calculated as number of hhs receiving CGP multiplied by average number of members in the hh. Plus the number of pensioners receiving the OAP. At baseline there were 100,000 household members in CGP and 85,000 OAP pensioners.</p>

title.narrative: PDI 3: Percentage of households receiving PA that are in poorest two quintiles of the population.

comment.narrative:
<p>Equity indicator. Not Achieved/Partially Achieved. Confirmed in Gov. Final Report. Newer households data not available, no changes in PA targeting procedures have taken place during the project.</p>

<p>Similar to above PDI 2. Data sources/old data.</p>

<p>For PA – new beneficiaries may have been selected from NISSA, but funds were not available to include them in the program so the effect may not be as pronounced as for PDI 2.</p>

title.narrative: PDI 2: Percentage of households receiving CGP that are in the poorest two quintiles of the population.

comment.narrative:
<p>Equity indicator. Not achieved. Confirmed by Gov. Final Report at 63.9%. Newer households data not available, but targeting of the CGP is expected to have improved since 2016 when NISSA PMT started to be used.</p>

<p>Household survey was supposed to produce fresher data.</p>

<p>The “actuals” are really from 2017, when NISSA was just getting started. Latest data is before NISSA started to be used, and improvements can be expected.</p>

title.narrative: An Integrated Managemeent Information System is adopted by MoSD for CGP, OVC, and PA

comment.narrative:
<p>Partially achieved. Gov. Final report reports this as:</p>
<p>“Only CGP and OVC modules have been developed for the MIS (except for the GRM). PA has no MIS. The issue of the support contract to complete all the modules has taken too long.”</p>

actual.value: CGP and OVC Bursary modules have been developed for the new IMIS. The PA modules are currently being developed.
